headline: Signs It Is Time to Upgrade Your Home Plumbing: When to Call a Pro
articleBody:
Upgrading your plumbing can completely transform how your kitchen or bathroom functions every day, but knowing when you need a licensed general contractor rather than a quick hand is vital. If your remodel involves moving supply lines, shifting drain locations, or rearranging your layout, casual handyman fixes will not cut it.

When Professional Guidance Helps
- Multiple fixtures are relocating: Moving a sink across the kitchen or shifting a shower requires re-routing concealed pipes within floors and walls.
- Walls and floors are opening up: Any project exposing subfloors or wall framing means structural considerations and building inspections come into play.
- Low pressure or old pipe materials: If your existing home has deteriorating supply lines or chronic drainage slow-downs, updating them during an active renovation saves immense money compared to tearing open walls later.
- Permit and code questions: Local building codes require strict rough-in inspections before any drywall goes up. 

Leaving concealed plumbing updates to a licensed team keeps your project safe, legal, and watertight.
